title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview
--------
This document consolidates Redwood Inferences company-wide policies and standardized processes for: access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees, managers, and approvers.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all full-time employees, contractors, and vendors operating under Redwood Inference.
Applies to systems and services owned by Redwood Inference and to vendor systems that process company data.

Responsibility and ownership
---------------------------
- People Ops: overall policy maintenance, travel & expense policy, templates and company-level approvals.
- Security & Compliance: RBAC policy, privileged access reviews, data classification and retention rules.
- Eng SRE / Eng Infra: change-management runbooks, maintenance windows, and deployment approvals.
- Finance & Legal: procurement thresholds, vendor contracts, and expense auditing.
- Managers: approve role-based access, training confirmations, and expense reports.

1) Access & Permissions
-----------------------
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access, auditable provisioning, and timely revocation.

Key principles:
- Least privilege: default to minimum access required for job function.
- Just-in-time (JIT) access: privileged actions should leverage JIT workflows where available.
- Separation of duties: approval and execution should be split where risk is material.
- Auditability: all privilege changes must be logged and reviewed quarterly.

Standard processes:
- Onboarding: Manager submits Access Request form (link: /confluence/policies-and-process/access-request-form) within 2 business days of hire start date. Security runs RBAC mapping within 3 business days.
- Role changes: Manager-approved change request; provisioning completed within 2 business days.
- Offboarding: People Ops triggers automated deprovisioning; all access revoked within 4 hours of termination for full-time, 24 hours for contractors unless otherwise specified.
- Privileged access: Requests for sensitive roles (DB admin, KMS admin) require Security approval plus manager sign-off and recorded justification.

Access review cadence:
- Quarterly automated reviews for all high-privilege groups.
- Annual company-wide entitlement review.

Escalation and exceptions:
- Temporary exceptions must include a justification, TTL (max 14 days without reapproval), and an owner. Exceptions are tracked in the Exceptions Registry. Security approval required for any exception beyond 30 days.

2) Change Management
--------------------
Purpose: Minimize production risk by standardizing deployment and infrastructure change workflows.

Change types and approvals:
- Standard change: pre-authorized routine operations (backups, small config tweaks). Requires owner notification and automated ticketing.
- Minor change: low risk, requires change owner and SRE review.
- Major change: any change that affects latency, capacity, data schema, or customer-facing behavior. Requires a Change Advisory Board (CAB) review and a rollback plan.

Process highlights:
1. Create change request in the Change Tracker (Jira project: CHG). Include impact, rollback, test plan, and owner.
2. SRE/Infra review for minor/major; Security review if identity/data is affected.
3. CAB approval for major changes; CAB meets weekly and asynchronously for urgent items.
4. Schedule changes during defined maintenance windows: Tue/Wed 02:00-05:00 UTC by default for low-impact infra changes; customer-impacting changes require scheduled customer notifications 72 hours in advance.
5. Post-change validation checklist and automated smoke tests must pass before closing the change.

Emergency changes:
- Follow the Emergency Change runbook: immediate notification to on-call SRE, post-implementation retrospective required within 72 hours.

3) Data Management
------------------
Purpose: Protect confidentiality, integrity, and availability of company and customer data while enabling product teams to operate.

Data classification:
- Public: safe for external distribution.
- Internal: for Redwood employees and vetted contractors.
- Confidential: sensitive business information, PII, or model training data.
- Restricted: regulated data requiring additional controls (e.g., customer-controlled data with contractual obligations).

Retention and deletion:
- Default retention: logs 90 days, analytics aggregates 2 years, backups 30 days unless specified.
- Data owners must define a retention policy at dataset creation; default retention applies when none is specified.
- Secure deletion: documented secure delete steps required for Confidential and Restricted data; Security must confirm deletion for regulated datasets.

Data access & handling:
- All access to Confidential/Restricted data requires documented business justification and Security approval.
- Use customer-managed encryption keys (CMKs) where contractually required.
- No sensitive data in plain text in Slack or email; use approved secure channels and redaction tools.

Monitoring and compliance:
- Automated DLP scans run weekly across storage buckets and repositories. Alerts routed to Security for triage.
- Periodic audits: internal quarterly checks and annual external audit for regulated customers.

4) Procurement & Expenses
-------------------------
Purpose: Ensure spend is approved, auditable, and aligned with budget.

Thresholds and approvers:
- Purchases < $1,000: manager approval.
- $1,000- $25,000: manager + finance approval.
- > $25,000: VP-level approval + finance and legal review; contractual terms require legal review.
- Cloud/Compute commits: requires Eng Infra signoff and Finance approval for multi-month/annual commitments.

Preferred vendors and purchasing flow:
1. Check the Approved Vendor List (AVL) before procuring.
2. Initiate Purchase Request in Procurement portal (link: /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement-portal). Attach quotes and SOWs.
3. Finance issues a PO for approved requests.

Expense policy highlights:
- Employees must submit expenses via the Expense System within 30 days of incurrence.
- Per-diem and reimbursement rates are specified in the Travel section below.
- Receipts required for all expenses > $25. Unreceipted expenses subject to manager/Finance review.

5) Vendor Management
--------------------
Purpose: Manage vendor risk, ensure contractual protections, and maintain vendor performance records.

Vendor classification:
- Low risk: commodity services with no access to sensitive data.
- Moderate risk: vendors with limited access to internal systems or non-sensitive data.
- High risk: vendors with access to Confidential/Restricted data, privileged system access, or who affect customer-facing services.

Onboarding process:
1. Vendor intake form submitted to Finance & Legal with vendor details, scope, and data access needs.
2. Security performs risk assessment and proposes controls (MFA, IP allowlists, encryption).
3. Legal reviews contract terms (SLA, indemnity, data processing addendum) before signature.
4. Vendor added to Vendor Registry and assigned an owner.

Ongoing management:
- Quarterly vendor performance reviews for high-risk vendors.
- Contract renewal timeline: start reviews 90 days before expiry.
- Access reviews: revoke or revalidate vendor access quarterly.

Termination:
- Offboarding checklist: access revoke, return or destruction of data, confirmation of final invoices, and contractual close-out. Legal & Security must confirm data disposition for high-risk vendors.

6) Travel Policy
----------------
Purpose: Provide clear, fair, and cost-conscious guidelines for business travel reimbursement.

Booking and approvals:
- All business travel requires manager pre-approval. Travel booked through the approved travel provider or Travel Portal.
- International travel for customer or on-prem engagements requires People Ops notification and any required visas or export-control checks.

Per-diem and reimbursement:
- Meals: up to $75/day in North America (receipts required for amounts > $25). Regions have different per-diem caps (see Travel Portal).
- Lodging: reasonable and mid-tier hotels; upgrades require manager justification.
- Air: economy for domestic flights; premium economy or business requires VP approval for flights > 8 hours.

Expense submission:
- Submit within 30 days. Include receipts and purpose. Corporate cards preferred for booking.

Safety and security:
- Employees must register high-risk travel with People Ops and follow travel advisories.

7) Internal Templates and Forms
------------------------------
Purpose: Standardize requests and approvals to reduce ambiguity and speed reviews.

Available templates (links):
- Access Request Form: /confluence/policies-and-process/access-request-form
- Change Request Template (CHG): /confluence/eng-platform/change-request-template
- Vendor Intake Form: /confluence/finance-and-legal/vendor-intake-form
- Expense Report Template: /confluence/finance-and-legal/expense-report-template

Template usage rules:
- Use the canonical template for each request type. Ad-hoc attachments are allowed but not as a substitute for required fields.
- Templates include required approvers and expected SLAs.

Governance, training, and exceptions
----------------------------------
- Policy reviews: Annual cadence; policy owners must present proposed changes to stakeholders during the March Governance week.
- Training: Mandatory policy acknowledgment and role-based training on access and data handling during onboarding. Refresher training annually.
- Exceptions: All exceptions must be captured in the Exceptions Registry with owner, TTL, and compensating controls. Long-running exceptions (>90 days) require exec-level sign-off.

Metrics and reporting
---------------------
- Quarterly metrics published: average time-to-provision access, number of outstanding exceptions, change success rate, vendor SLA compliance, expense audit rate.
- Security publishes monthly access anomalies and retention audit findings.

Appendices
----------
A. Maintenance windows and contact list (SRE on-call, Security Pager, People Ops escalation).
B. Glossary of terms (RBAC, JIT, CMK, DLP, CAB).
C. Quick checklist: onboarding access, procurement request, vendor intake, emergency change flow.
